newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to hit 3.0 pct/GDP deficit goal - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Germany to hit 3.0 pct/GDP deficit goal - spokesman.

text.p: German government spokesman Peter Hausmann said on Monday that Bonn would cut the budget deficit to exactly three percent of gross domestic product this year to qualify for Europe's single currency.
"Our goal is 3.0 percent and we will reach that," Hausmann told the government's regular news conference.
Germany to hit 3.0 pct/GDP deficit goal-spokesman

Asked to comment on France's chances of cutting government borrowing enough to meet the terms of the Maastricht treaty, Hausmann said: "What is important is that we all do our homework. It would be inappropriate to offer any advice."
French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn on Monday announced a round of tax hikes aimed at cutting France's budget deficit, now running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent, by 0.4 percentage points.

Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier he did not consider the tax hikes as one-off creative accounting to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU). He said he had been assured by Strauss-Kahn that Paris would fulfil the EMU deficit goal next year.
Waigel, speaking in Munich, declined to speculate on France's chances of meeting the Maastricht criteria, but said it would be difficult to imagine EMU beginning without Germany or France.
